first.rationale: Current metrics show onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that onboarding simplification and signup field reduction drive measurable activation lift in SMB segments. Memory_91 shows activation messaging compounds this effect. Rather than chase competitor pricing (which threatens margin and long-term value), addressing the activation and completion declines directly targets sustainable qualified revenue. Verify memory_31 (signup field reduction) and memory_91 (activation messaging) to confirm whether a combined approach is viable. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding can be instrumented in one week, isolates the causal factor, and aligns with the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue over tactical pricing wars.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memory_31 (signup simplification +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue) and memory_91 (activation messaging +6% activation, +11% week-one engagement, +1% retention lift) are reliable. However, memory_31's modest retention impact (-1%) and SMB-only constraint present risk given current competitive pressure on price-sensitive segments. Memory_91 shows broader applicability with positive retention signal (+1%) and strong engagement lift. Since activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ, activation messaging directly addresses the engagement gap without introducing pricing or retention risk. This preserves sustainable qualified revenue by improving product value realization for existing funnel rather than competing on price or restructuring flows mid-cycle. Standard experiment scales to all segments and can ship this week.
